questions.question: What does a Jupyter notebook add to an ordinary Python file?
options: Interactive code, Markdown, and outputs
A replacement for the operating system shell
A database that stores model weights automatically
A compiler that turns Python into Rust
questions.explanation: Notebook cells share a running kernel, so code, Markdown, and visible outputs can be developed together. The notebook does not replace the Python interpreter or provide automatic model storage.

questions.question: In the lesson's NotebookKernel, what remains after executing samples = [2, 4, 8] in one cell?
options: Only the printed text remains; variables are discarded
It keeps samples available to later cells
The kernel writes samples to a new Git branch
The next cell starts in a separate process by default
questions.explanation: NotebookKernel keeps a namespace between execute calls. A later cell can evaluate sum(samples) until restart clears that namespace.

questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes %timeit from %%time?
options: %timeit displays plots; %%time saves them as PNG files
%timeit restarts the kernel; %%time preserves variables
Repeated line timing versus one cell timing
They are aliases with different spellings
questions.explanation: Repeated measurements make %timeit useful for small operations. %%time measures one complete cell, which is more suitable for observing a training or data-loading pass.

questions.question: A notebook succeeds only after you ran cell 7 before cell 3. What should you try before sharing it?
options: Add more output to cell 7 without restarting
Copy the hidden variable into every Markdown cell
Turn off the kernel so the stale state remains
Restart, then Run All
questions.explanation: Restarting removes variables created by accidental execution order. Run All then exposes missing imports, definitions, or data preparation in the order a reader will follow.

questions.question: In the demo, what does kernel.execute('samples') return immediately after kernel.restart()?
options: A CellResult with a NameError
The list [2, 4, 8]
An empty display value with no error
A Git conflict marker
questions.explanation: restart replaces the namespace with only the notebook marker. Since samples has not been defined again, execute reports the NameError rather than a stale value.

questions.question: You have explored a preprocessing idea in a notebook and now need a nightly training job. What is the sound handoff?
options: Keep hidden cell order and ask the scheduler to run cells by their visible position
Extract reusable code into a tested script
Paste the final plot into a shell script and remove the data-loading code
Export only the notebook outputs because the source cells are no longer needed
questions.explanation: A scheduled job needs an explicit, repeatable entrypoint. Extracting reusable code into a script makes imports, arguments, and tests visible while the notebook can still document experiments.
